topic: Flying fish glide over the waves
script: Some fish can fly through the air to escape hungry predators. Flying fish leap out of the water and spread their long fins like wings. They glide rather than flap. By beating their tails on the surface, they can stretch a glide to over 200 meters. They often flee tuna, dolphins and other fast hunters. In 2008, a film crew in Japan recorded one gliding for about 45 seconds. Follow Pixel Abyss for more strange facts from the deep.
